title: Tabella del dieci
instruction: Metti i dischetti nella tabella — e guarda quanto posto resta libero.
trayAriaOne: La vaschetta — ancora uno da mettere
gateBody: Una raccolta di tabelle già pronte — lo stesso numero disposto in cinque modi, gli amici del dieci, coppie da confrontare e i numeri da undici a diciannove su tutte e due le tabelle. Tieni da parte le tabelle che costruisci e ritrovale quando ti servono.
_notes: PANEL: native linguist + scuola primaria (classe 1ª-2ª) maths teacher + native B2C education-marketing writer. Rebuilt, not translated. We audited the English source and the model as instructed; findings below are ordered defects-first.

=== BUILT AGAINST _source-en.json sha1 857298096155c8face59c85a764c277dfc6f746f — 30 KEYS, NOT 31. ⚠ THE SOURCE WAS REWRITTEN UNDER US MID-RUN (mtime 04:09:41, after our read; sibling panels de/fr/da/nl were being written at the same time). We caught it only because a key-count assertion against the source failed at the end; a panel that had written its file straight out of its first read would have shipped a key the tool no longer has, with the wrong gate copy, and nothing downstream compares a locale against the source. Three edits landed: (a) routinesBtn was DELETED — we had authored 'Sequenze' for it and have removed it; (b) fieldTwentyField went from 'Field of twenty' to 'Frame of twenty'; (c) gateBody dropped 'and print the one on screen' for 'come back to them'. RECOMMEND the applier hash-pin the source, or that the panel brief carry the hash, because a concurrent fan-out over a mutable source is exactly the shape that ships one locale built against a different spec from the other ten.

=== DEFECT 0, and the source edit above fixes it — THE OLD gateBody SOLD A FREE AFFORDANCE INSIDE THE PAID GATE. It ended 'Keep your own frames, and print the one on screen', while :1154-1161 rules Print explicitly NOT locked, operator-ruled, on the grounds that this is TOOL_KEYS[0] and 'locking the first thing a signed-out teacher reaches for is never gate the first affordance in slow motion'. A gate body that lists printing as a reason to pay contradicts the tool's own ruling and, worse, teaches a teacher that the chip she can already press is behind a paywall. The revised EN is correct and our Italian follows it: 'Tieni da parte le tabelle che costruisci e ritrovale quando ti servono' — persistence only, which is the thing that is actually gated. We flag it because the old wording was live in all eleven locales and the other ten panels may have inherited it.

NOTE ON fieldTwentyField — the EN edit 'Field of twenty' → 'Frame of twenty' unifies the noun, and Italian was already there: our set uses 'tabella' for all four fields, so the twenty is 'Tabella del venti'. No change was needed, which is the check passing rather than a coincidence — a locale that had rendered 'Field' as a second noun (campo) would now be inconsistent with its own head term.

=== DEFECT 1 (ENGLISH SOURCE, ships in all 11) — trayAria is ungrammatical at {n}=1. 'The tray — 1 counters left'. This is not an edge case: the tray passes through 1 on the way to full in EVERY field, so it is reached in the tool's own headline routine ('take one out, put it in'). The first-pass Italian inherited it verbatim ('restano 1 gettoni'). Our rebuild is agreement-free by construction: '{n} ancora da mettere' is correct at 1 and at 19. RECOMMEND the EN be re-cut the same way (e.g. 'The tray — {n} still to place'), and that every other locale be re-checked for it — Romance and Nordic panels will all have inherited the plural verb.

=== DEFECT 1, RESOLVED — trayAriaOne was added to the tool after our read and is the fix; the source is now 31 keys and the tray has three forms (empty / one / many), selected at ten-frame.js:1050-1052. THE THREE MUST CARRY ONE NOUN: the tray is one of the tool's three named parts (:15-16) and a part that changes its name with its contents is not a part. In Italian the mismatch ran the opposite way to most locales — the hand-seeded SINGULAR already said 'la vaschetta' (correct), while the shipped trayAria and trayEmptyAria still say 'il vassoio', which is the first-pass noun we rejected as fraction-kitchen's and money-core's. All three in this file are 'la vaschetta'. ⚠ SECOND AGREEMENT AXIS, worth naming for the other panels: the singular must also agree with the panel's COUNTER noun, not only carry its tray noun — 'ancora uno da mettere' is masculine because our counter is 'un dischetto'; a locale that chose a feminine counter (ficha, brikke) needs 'una'/its own form, and no gate can see that. The word order also keeps the set parallel: 'ancora … da mettere' is shared with the many form, so the three readings sound like one instrument at three fill levels.

=== DEFECT 2 (CODE, ten-frame.js:1051) — {n} and {left} are replaced NON-globally while {cap} is global. The line is msg.replace('{n}', …).replace(/\{cap\}/g, …).replace('{left}', …). The asymmetry looks accidental rather than designed. Any locale whose natural phrasing repeats {n} — and a 'still N … N out of cap' construction is plausible in Italian and very likely in Finnish — silently ships a literal '{n}' into a live region, where no visual gate can see it. Make all three global. We routed around it (each of our templates uses {n} once), so this is a report, not a blocker.

=== DEFECT 3 (MODEL/UX, ten-frame.js:473-479) — an ordinary tap destroys the setup for the tool's own signature routine. tap() on a FILLED cell does m &= (1<<i)-1, i.e. it clears that ordinal AND every ordinal above it. On a canonical board that is exactly the fill-level behaviour promised by T4. On a SCATTERED board it is not: with {0,3,7} occupied, tapping the counter at 3 removes TWO counters, not one. The header's routine is 'Scatter them. Is it still seven? — hands up, argue, then Tidy.' A child who touches one of the scattered counters during the argument silently collapses the scatter, and the announcement reports the new number as if nothing unusual happened. The empty branch carries the comment 'it never relocates a counter a child has placed'; the filled branch has no equivalent guard. Shift-tap (toggleOne) is the correct single-counter gesture but is not discoverable on a whiteboard. We are not proposing a fix — that is a design ruling — but the class of interaction is worth the operator's attention because it is aimed at the one routine the tool exists for.

=== DEFECT 4 (SHIPPED ITALIAN) — keepsBtn was 'I miei quadri', the only string in the Italian set using 'quadro'. Every other Italian string in this tool uses 'tabella' (title, all four field chips, frameAria, numeralAria, gateTitle). 'Quadro de dez' is the shipped PORTUGUESE head term for this tool — the Italian first pass appears to have taken the Portuguese noun. Fixed to 'Le mie tabelle', which also matches the house Keeps convention ('Le mie parole', 'Le mie stime', 'Le mie serie', 'I miei timer').

=== DEFECT 5 (LEXICON) — the English noun census found 'counter' and 'tray' free; in ITALIAN both are occupied, and this is §23.6's 'the obvious word is already taken' exactly. gettone is shipped by part-whole-frame ('Sposta un gettone' — its SOLE affordance), by sound-boxes ('Metti un gettone in una casella per ogni suono', plus 'Forma gettone' and 'Colore gettone' as settings labels) and by lids. sound-boxes is the worst possible neighbour: same gesture, same catalogue — put a token into a box. vassoio is shipped by fraction-kitchen (inside a PAID GATE string, 'Riempi il vassoio') and by money-core. Both had to go, and neither collision is visible from the English side.

RULING — the counters are DISCHETTI. Asked directly: yes, a primaria teacher says 'gettoni'. It is the right word and it is not available (above). Of what remains, dischetto is the honest second: Italian didactic kits do ship 'dischetti colorati', the tool literally draws a disc (disc() at :946), it is free across all 47 tools, and Italian children meet the word early through calcio ('dal dischetto'). REJECTED: pedina — free, but it is a board-game pawn, i.e. a piece that MOVES ALONG A PATH; that is ordinal, and this tool's whole thesis is cardinal. It also drags a player/turn/winner frame into a tool that refuses competition. REJECTED: bottone — concrete and free, but the cells ARE <button> elements and every one of them is announced; 'un bottone' inside the accessible name of a button is a collision a sighted review cannot see. REJECTED: segnalino (open-number-line), tessera (word-builder-core), tappo/tappi (free, but a bottle cap is improvised material, not an instrument).

RULING — the tray is LA VASCHETTA. It is the exact object: the plastic tub Italian primaria keeps its materials in, so the sentence 'prendi un dischetto dalla vaschetta' is something a teacher already says. It is free across all 47 tools, and it is bowl-shaped, which the code requires — :762 'You reach into the bowl.' REJECTED: vassoio (taken twice, see above), ciotola (measurement-bench), scatola (letter-tiles), barattolo (class-timer, estimation-jar, name-sticks), cestino (fraction-kitchen — and in any UI 'cestino' is the wastebasket, i.e. the counters you took out were thrown away, which is the opposite of the meaning), piattino (free, but counters roll off a saucer; the picture fights the model).

RULING — the tidy verb is ALLINEA. The prompt asks what the verb is for making a scattered set line up. In class you would say 'mettiamoli in ordine' or 'sistemateli', but as a chip label: 'Riordina' is shipped by center-board and 'Sistema' by rekenrek, and this is the tool's signature control — the only operation that moves a counter without adding or removing one — so it should own its own verb. 'Allinea' is free, is one chip-sized word, and names precisely what the class watches happen: the counters march into line from the start. Consequently saidTidied ends '…allineati' (masculine plural, agreeing with i dischetti) rather than the first pass's 'riordinata' (feminine singular, agreeing with la tabella). That is also more accurate: what moved was the counters, not the frame.

RULING — saidFull is 'Al completo', not 'Piena'. The first pass ('Piena, {cap} su {cap}') and 'riordinata' both silently GENDER-LOCK to the locked title's noun: they are grammatical only for as long as the frame noun is feminine. That is an invisible dependency between a string and a value the panel is forbidden to change. 'Al completo' is invariant, idiomatic for a full container, and removes the last gender coupling in the set.

FIXED IDIOM — 'i compagni del dieci' is not what this is called in Italy. The idiom is GLI AMICI DEL DIECI (cf. sv 'tiokamraterna', es 'los amigos del diez', nl 'de vriendjes van tien' — every other locale in gateBody already has its own idiom; Italian was the calque). Applied to gateBody.

OTHER FIRST-PASS STRINGS REPLACED BECAUSE THEY WERE ALREADY TAKEN IN ITALIAN: 'Completa' (fillBtn) — number-talk-easel, story-line, wodb → 'Riempi tutto'. 'A coppie' (orderPairs) — class-timer, hush-owl → 'A due a due', which is better anyway: it is what an Italian class actually chants when counting in twos, and it reads as a rhythm rather than as a layout setting. (routinesBtn's 'Percorsi' also collided — letter-studio — and we had replaced it with 'Sequenze'; the key was then deleted from the source, so the ruling is recorded here only in case the chip returns.) 'Conserva' was considered for gateBody and rejected (calendar-wall, name-sticks) in favour of 'Tieni da parte'.

NAMING HAZARD, RECORDED — do NOT name fieldTwentyField 'la linea del 20', however tempting the recognition. It is Camillo Bortolato's registered Erickson product name, and it would also collide head-on with number-line's Italian head term 'Linea dei numeri'. The geometry is the right geometry; the name is not ours to take. 'Tabella del venti' keeps the tool's own lexicon and is unambiguous.

HEAD-TERM NOTE (no action — title is locked and we did not touch it). 'Tabella' is now the most loaded noun in the Italian catalogue. 'Tabellone' is shipped by blending-board, center-board, letter-tiles, syllable-splitter and heart-words; and number-talk-easel ships 'Doppia tabella' plus 'Tabelle, abaco e oggetti fanno parte di Premium' — i.e. the easel's Italian repertoire names OUR head term directly. Per the fence ruling at :117-124 this is legal (the easel's frame is aria-hidden — it is a picture; ours is a keyboard-operable grid, and what was subtracted was the VERB, not the noun), so nothing here needs changing. It is recorded so a future reviewer does not rediscover it as a defect. Separately: 'tabella' carries a faint pull toward 'tabellina' (times table) for an Italian adult — not for a six-year-old, and not enough to reopen a locked indexed head term.

GRIGLIA / SCHEDA — confirmed dead for this tool, for the reason given: 'griglia di valutazione' and 'scheda di valutazione' are assessment paperwork, and a free-play instrument that refuses to grade anything must not wear an assessment noun. Neither appears in any tool's Italian strings today. Recording it so the next Italian panel does not propose 'griglia del dieci', which is otherwise the obvious calque of 'ten-frame'.

=== BORTOLATO / GEOMETRY_BY_LOCALE — our recommendation for the operator (:228-231; we did not change the file). RECOMMEND it: { single: 'ten', twenty: 'twentyfield' }. The twenty is the confident half and it is a fact about the material, not a preference: Bortolato's 'linea del 20' (Erickson) is the dominant numbers-to-20 apparatus in Italian primaria, and its structure is TWENTY IN TWO ROWS OF TEN, each row broken 5+5 to mirror the two hands. That is twentyfield — one 2x10 block with a five-break — and it is NOT twentypair, the American double ten-frame, which no Italian material presents. An Italian class reads 13 as one complete row of ten and three, which is exactly the base-ten reading the header says the material exists to produce. So Italy lands on the same field as Germany, by a different national route. On the SINGLE we deliberately stop short of the stronger claim. Bortolato-true would be 'tenrow': the first row of the linea del 20 IS ten in a row with a five-break, and the hands metaphor is a row, not a 2x5 block. We do not recommend it as the default for two reasons. First, practical and measured in this file: tenrow is ten cells WIDE, and :738-740 says the scroller exists precisely so a ten-wide field can keep a 34px cell on a phone — defaulting an entire locale to the one field that can need horizontal scroll on arrival is a real cost paid by every visitor. Second, the tool is called 'Tabella del dieci' and a teacher who searched that term should see the frame the term names; tenrow is one tap away, permanently, as its own chip. If the operator wants full Bortolato alignment and accepts the phone cost, single: 'tenrow' is the coherent alternative — both rows of one national artefact — but it is a product ruling, not ours.

CONSTRAINTS CHECKED: title unchanged and byte-identical to the locked value. No verdict, score, praise or error word anywhere. No string asks a question or demands an answer — instruction and gateBody are both descriptive. Placeholders: {n} in filledAt/trayAria/numeralAria; {n},{cap} in saidBoard/saidTidied; {n},{cap},{left} in saidRoom; {cap} twice in saidFull; {field},{n},{cap} in saidField; and in no other string. gateCta contains 'Insegnante' and matches part-whole-frame's shipped wording exactly, which is the house lexicon for this plan. saidTidied states the invariant explicitly ('Ancora …' = still), which is the only way a screen-reader user learns that Allinea did not change the number. No apostrophes were needed anywhere in the set, so the curly-vs-straight question does not arise; the only non-ASCII characters are the accented a in 'già' and the em dashes, which match the sibling tools.
